headline: Math is nearly solved while agents on real work lag behind
outlook: Math is where the past year has moved fastest: models have closed 95% of the remaining headroom on math benchmarks, FrontierMath crossed 90% in September, and its hardest tier has now been scored at 100%. Practical agent work is the clear laggard, with only about a third of headroom closed, the Remote Labor Index at 20.8% and OSWorld 2 at 31.4%, even as a run of September releases nudged up records on APEX-Agents and coding benchmarks. The bridge between those two worlds is task length: the longest tasks models can handle now stand at 17.4 hours and have been doubling roughly every 4.2 months, which on current trends points to a full 40-hour work-week around December, though the likely range runs to August 2027. Not everything is on schedule, since Terminal-Bench, GeoBench and the push for GPQA-level performance under a cent per million tokens have all fallen behind their fitted trends, a reminder that last-mile gains and price floors can stall. With past ranges catching the real date only 59% of the time, the safest read for the next year is that reasoning-heavy benchmarks will keep falling quickly while sustained, real-world agent work remains the frontier to watch.
